scope.description: User-directed Canada-first deep research on Dominion Dynamics, covering its Arctic autonomy, sensing, command-and-control, aerospace, sovereign simulation, procurement-intelligence, field-deployment, partnership, and Canadian operating evidence.

source.title: Building Next-Generation Defence Systems
source.locator: Mission, Platforms, AI Native, Interoperable, Modular, AuraNet, Contact, and Join our team sections
source.summary: Dominion's canonical site describes a Canadian defence-technology portfolio spanning integrated autonomy, sensing, communications, command and control, edge data fusion, modular integration, and the AuraNet platform for extreme and infrastructure-constrained operations.

leads.evidenceLocator: Canonical platform pages, official company newsroom, company-issued releases, live AURION service, and current Government of Canada founder profile
followUpQuestions: Should reviewers retain AURION inside the same defence-prime profile or treat it as an adjacent ecosystem-intelligence product?
Should the Scout Autonomous Collaborative Platform remain a program-level capability until product specifications become more public?
How prominently should company-reported Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT field activity appear when no matching government deployment source was located in this run?
Should a future review add an exact Kanata facility address if a canonical company contact or facility page publishes it?
leads.candidateCapabilityName: Dominion integrated Arctic autonomy and command portfolio
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Complementary official sources identify Dominion Dynamics as an Ottawa-headquartered Canadian defence-technology company developing AuraNet data fusion and command-and-control software, Arctic sensing and communications integration, the Scout autonomous collaborative aircraft program, a sovereign AI simulation environment with Denvr, and AURION procurement intelligence. Company reports also document Canadian Rangers field activity and a new Kanata manufacturing facility.
